markdown_report:
Select a **catalog-competition audit for the corrected GRU4Rec**. At 0% progress, identifying whether sampled separation conceals omitted competitors is a feasible next step before another training intervention. No validation improvement is established.

Three starting insights guide this choice. First, supplied training margins are generally positive, but they measure sampled discrimination; further margin growth need not improve HR@10. Second, latest-item deletion causes larger rank changes than oldest-item deletion, demonstrating temporal reliance without establishing that stronger recency would help. Third, module checks pass while generated-predictor parity remains unverified; deployment consistency is still an open implementation question.

Three literature insights sharpen the direction. Hidasi and Czapp [1] show how sampled evaluation can distort catalog rankings, motivating explicit competitor counts. Pereira et al. [2] distinguish sampling reliability dimensions, motivating analytic sampling probabilities alongside observed ranks. Prakash et al. [3] report popularity disparities hidden by aggregate metrics, motivating training-frequency strata without assuming the same disparities occur here.

The framework separates three research directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competition | Sampled margins | Exact eligible-catalog ranks | Training-prefix generalization |
| Memory | History perturbations | Lag-dependent state/score sensitivity | Useful versus merely retained information |
| Optimization | Aggregate losses | Position-group gradient comparisons | Local opposition versus harmful interference |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores denote originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more engineering.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog-competition audit [1–3] | 3/7/3 | Directly measures omitted competition; established mathematics and chunked scoring make implementation practical | Primarily a diagnostic adaptation; catalog scoring costs time and proves no improvement |
| Lag-dependent GRU sensitivity [4] | 4/6/6 | Separates state retention from target discrimination and supports later gate interventions | Attribution depends on perturbations; recurrent differentiation requires careful engineering |
| Position-group gradient audit [5] | 4/6/5 | Locates opposing updates within one network using standard autograd | Gradient conflict is established and does not establish harmful generalization; parameter-group comparisons add overhead |

For the selected audit, freeze each category model and use at most 256 training prefixes with aligned targets. Exclude original-history items from competitors, retain the target once, and score the eligible training catalog in chunks. Count competitors preceding the target under descending score and ascending item-ID ties; report exact rank, target-minus-tenth-competitor margin, and analytic probability of hitting a uniformly sampled 100-item diagnostic set. Stratify by training popularity and history length; report undefined cases and support.

Keep these descriptive results separate from pinned validation selection. Anonymous prefixes receive no user-bootstrap intervals. Preserve diagnostic APIs, left-padding alignment, fresh recurrent states, four-category routing, and one checkpoint per category. Verify the actual generated predictor when callable; otherwise retain the parity limitation. All diagnostic GPU time consumes the shared budget.

idea.description: Add a bounded, training-only catalog-competition audit to the existing GRU4Rec diagnostic adapter. For each selected prefix, score the eligible catalog using its single trained category model, measure exact target rank and omitted competition, and calculate the target's hit probability under uniform sampling of 99 unique negatives.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish training separation and temporal reliance, but neither establishes catalog-wide ranking quality or validation improvement. An exact competition audit tests a distinct explanation for apparently healthy sampled margins without assuming that stronger recency, larger margins, or a different backbone is desirable.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions, preserving existing probes and all ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Keep the public loader yield (None, sequence, positive, negative).

Use a separate diagnostic RNG seeded 42 without consuming training RNG draws. Cap collection at ten batches and 256 prefixes per category. Use only training histories and aligned training targets; do not inspect validation or test files for this audit. Anonymous prefixes are descriptive observations, not identified independent users. Save the protocol and bounded results beneath the current trial directory.

Run under eval and no_grad, restoring the prior model mode in finally. Each independent history starts from fresh recurrent state. Gather features at the maximum nonzero sequence index, never nonpadding count minus one. Skip empty histories and zero aligned targets with explicit counts.

Define competitor eligibility from real observed training-catalog IDs, excluding reserved tokens, the target and the original observed prefix. Include the target exactly once even when it occurs in the prefix. This is a declared diagnostic population, not a claim to reproduce host eligibility. Unobserved competitors are not verified dislikes. Use the identical eligible population for exact ranks and diagnostic sampling probabilities.

Score catalog items in chunks through predict_score(features, items). Count competitors preceding the target under descending score and ascending item-ID ties. Maintain the ten highest-ranked competitors without retaining a full prefix-by-catalog score matrix. Report target rank, eligible competitor count, outranking competitor count, target score minus tenth-highest competitor score, and training-frequency popularity strata. Return null with reasons when fewer than ten competitors exist or scores are nonfinite.

For N eligible competitors and M preceding the target, sample n=min(99,N) unique negatives. The number preceding the target follows Hypergeometric(N,M,n), so diagnostic hit probability is P(X<=9). Use scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf with explicit handling of N=0. Report actual candidate counts. Analytic probabilities describe the declared diagnostic sampling process; they are not host validation HR@10. A small fixed set of diagnostic redraws can cross-check implementation, but is unnecessary for estimating a probability already available analytically.

Define popularity bands from training interaction counts only, with deterministic item-ID tie breaking. Report support and descriptive prefix means; omit user-bootstrap intervals unless stable user IDs are actually available. Do not optimize these diagnostics or simulator feedback as selection metrics. No unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility or mood may be inferred.

Keep the corrected GRU4Rec architecture, objective, optimizer and inference unchanged for this diagnostic proposal. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, 200 batches per epoch, maximum 200 epochs, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], fixed splits and the pinned evaluator. Retain exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint per category, without fusion, averaging or checkpoint reuse. Charge diagnostics and debugging to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Verify actual generated working/predict.py scores and category routing against selected checkpoints when an executable predictor interface is available, including empty and single-item histories and different left-padding widths. Module serialization parity alone does not verify the predictor writer. No execution, parity success, runtime affordability or validation gain is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        prior_mode = self.view.model.training
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                results = retain_existing_measured_probes(train_loader)
                for row in bounded_training_prefixes(train_loader,
                                                     max_batches=10,
                                                     max_prefixes=256):
                    positions = nonzero_indices(row.sequence)
                    if not positions:
                        record_skip('empty_history')
                        continue
                    t = max(positions)
                    target = int(row.positive[t])
                    if target == 0:
                        record_skip('missing_target')
                        continue
                    features = self.view.log2feats(row.sequence[None])[0, t]
                    target_score = score_one(features, target)
                    excluded = set(row.sequence[positions]) | reserved_ids | {target}
                    eligible = training_catalog_ids_without(excluded)
                    N, M = 0, 0
                    top_competitors = bounded_topk(10)
                    for items in chunks(eligible):
                        scores = self.view.predict_score(features, items)
                        require_finite(scores)
                        precedes = ((scores > target_score) |
                                    ((scores == target_score) & (items < target)))
                        N += len(items)
                        M += int(precedes.sum())
                        top_competitors.update(scores, items)
                    n = min(99, N)
                    hit_probability = (1.0 if N == 0 else
                                       hypergeom.cdf(min(9, n), N, M, n))
                    record(rank=1 + M, competitors=N, preceding=M,
                           diagnostic_candidate_count=1+n,
                           diagnostic_hit_probability=hit_probability,
                           target_minus_tenth_competitor=(
                               target_score - top_competitors.score_at(10)
                               if N >= 10 else None),
                           training_popularity_band=band(target),
                           history_length=len(positions))
                return {'metrics': aggregate_with_support(results),
                        'metric_definitions': explicit_protocol_and_limits()}
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(prior_mode)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
                           raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
                           distinguish_diagnostics_from_validation=True,
                           forbid_unsupported_causal_or_preference_claims=True)

originality.positive: Combines exact eligible-catalog competition, analytic sampled-hit probabilities and popularity strata within the required GRU4Rec diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Exact ranks, hypergeometric sampling analysis and popularity breakdowns are established techniques; the contribution is their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish easy sampled discrimination from substantial omitted competition and motivate focused subsequent loss or sampling experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix findings may reflect memorization, and diagnostic improvements need not improve the pinned macro validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing scoring hooks, bounded top-k accumulation and a standard hypergeometric distribution without changing architecture or checkpoints.
code_difficulty.negative: Catalog scoring adds runtime, and eligibility, deterministic ties, mode restoration and predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp (2023): evaluation flaws in recommender systems
contributions: Demonstrates distortions introduced by sampled evaluation in GRU4Rec experiments.
Relates sampled-hit probabilities to full rank through a hypergeometric distribution.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed training-prefix audit predicts improvement on this benchmark.
Analytic probabilities require matching the declared eligibility, sampling and ranking rules.

related_work.title: Pereira et al. (2025): reliability of sampling-based recommendation evaluation
contributions: Examines sampling reliability through fidelity, resolution, robustness and recovery of model rankings.
limitations: Does not supply results for the four category models considered here.
Sampling reliability analysis does not itself improve a recommender.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): popularity disparities in sequential recommendation
contributions: Reports head, middle and tail disparities obscured by aggregate sequential-recommendation metrics.
Investigates popularity effects associated with random training negatives.
limitations: Reported disparities cannot be assumed to hold for the supplied GRU4Rec checkpoints.
Popularity strata describe behavior without identifying user preferences or causal mechanisms.

related_work.title: Gating creates slow modes and controls phase-space complexity in GRUs and LSTMs
contributions: Connects recurrent gating to memory timescales and dynamical behavior.
Motivates separating hidden-state retention from downstream score sensitivity.
limitations: Gate behavior alone does not establish useful memory or recommendation accuracy.
Does not validate the proposed GRU4Rec sensitivity audit.

related_work.title: Gradient-conflict research referenced in the supplied search results (2024)
contributions: Motivates examining competing updates within shared model parameters.
limitations: The proposed sequence-position adaptation remains unvalidated.
Negative gradient cosine is local opposition and does not establish harmful generalization.
